---
title: "VRAM Reduction"
---

## What — Random Projection Sketch

Per-sample gradient storage for ShortcutScore computation causes CUDA OOM on GPU servers (14.6 GB for 64 samples). Random projection sketches compress each gradient from $\mathbb{R}^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^k$ ($k \ll d$), reducing VRAM by ~36,000x.

## Why — The OOM Bottleneck

| Component | Size | VRAM |
|-----------|------|------|
| Model parameters | ~19M params | 76 MB |
| Single gradient vector | 19M floats x 4 bytes | 76 MB |
| Batch of 64 x 3 types | 64 x 3 x 76 MB | **14.6 GB** |
| + model + activations | — | **~25-28 GB** |

The NL config (163M params) is worse: 652 MB per gradient vector.

<details>
<summary><strong>How — Johnson-Lindenstrauss Sketch Algorithm</strong></summary>

For each projection direction $z_j$ ($j = 0, \ldots, k-1$):

1. Generate random vector $z_j \sim N(0, I_d)$ via CPU RNG (never stored on GPU)
2. Perturb model: $\theta \leftarrow \theta + \varepsilon z_j$
3. Forward pass on batch: get per-sample losses $L^+_{\text{full}}, L^+_{\text{ans}}, L^+_{\text{reason}}$
4. Perturb model: $\theta \leftarrow \theta - 2\varepsilon z_j$
5. Forward pass: get $L^-_{\text{full}}, L^-_{\text{ans}}, L^-_{\text{reason}}$
6. Restore: $\theta \leftarrow \theta + \varepsilon z_j$
7. Compute sketch: $s_{\text{full}}[:,j] = (L^+_{\text{full}} - L^-_{\text{full}}) / (2\varepsilon)$

**Total**: $2k$ forward passes per batch (independent of batch size $B$).

**Memory savings**:

| Component | Current | With Sketch (k=128) |
|-----------|---------|---------------------|
| Per-sample gradient | 76 MB | 0.5 KB |
| Batch of 64 x 3 types | 14.6 GB | ~0.1 MB |
| **Reduction factor** | — | **~36,000x** |

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>How — Approximation Quality</strong></summary>

By the Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma, cosine similarities are preserved:

$$\cos(g_{\text{full},i}, g_V) \approx \cos(s_{\text{full},i}, s_V)$$

with error $O(1/\sqrt{k})$:

- $k = 128$: ~4% error
- $k = 512$: ~2% error
- $k = 1024$: ~1.5% error

The downstream task (binary shortcut classification) tolerates this approximation well.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>How — Configuration</strong></summary>

| Parameter | Default | Range | Effect |
|-----------|---------|-------|--------|
| `sketch_k` | 128 | [64, 1024] | Projection dimension |
| `sketch_epsilon` | 1e-3 | [1e-4, 1e-2] | Finite-difference step |
| `sketch_seed` | 0 | — | Base RNG seed for reproducibility |

- Canonical location: `src/utils/gradient_ops.py`
- Key functions: `_apply_perturbation()`, `compute_sample_sketches_batched()`, `sketch_gradient_vector()`

</details>
